biggest_catch: This only makes sense if you are already a paying Prime member: the $150 gift card arrives instantly on approval with no spending requirement, but if you would not otherwise pay for Prime, the membership cost eats the bonus. Year-one math: $150 gift card minus the $0 annual fee leaves $150 net, before any Prime subscription cost. Only claim this if you were already going to keep your Prime membership; never pay for Prime just for the bonus. The gift card loads to your Amazon account's Gift Card Balance on approval, and Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern applies.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway: this one has no spending requirement, but do not pay for a Prime membership you would not otherwise buy just to get the $150.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.
